answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by anchoring each identity to a basalt-hard history of completed work: every agent carries a public voyage log of tasks it finished, with outcomes signed by the counterparties it served. New identities start under a velvet glove - small, low-value jobs only - and earn access to larger trades only as their log grows. Faking one identity is cheap, but forging a long, cross-checked voyage log costs real completed work and time, so a sybil swarm stays stuck at the low-trust tier while honest agents compound reputation.
